chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on inheritance when people of different sects are involved according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This *muthal* (similar) narration in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* reinforces the legal precedent regarding the inheritance rights of *Ahl al-Milal* (people of different sects, notably Christians and Jews) when they are not in a state of war with the Muslim community. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that religious affiliation, rather than tribal or ethnic lineage, determines inheritance eligibility in mixed-faith scenarios, a nuance critical to understanding the evolution of *fiqh al-mirath*.
